mainEntity.name: How long does it take to see results from local search work?

acceptedAnswer.text: The timeline depends on where your profile and website start. Profile corrections, such as fixing a category or a mismatched phone number, can be reflected in a few weeks once Google reprocesses the listing. New community pages and content usually take longer, because Google has to crawl and evaluate them over time. Reviews build gradually as closings happen. A builder should expect steady progress over several months rather than an overnight change, and should judge progress by the leads that come in from specific communities and sources.

mainEntity.name: Should I list my model home address on my Google profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the model is a staffed sales location with posted hours that match what you publish. A buyer who visits the address should find a sales team and the homes you describe. If the model is closed most of the year or is only open by appointment, you can list it as a service area or set the hours to reflect appointments. The key rule is accuracy. Google compares the listing against your website and against what visitors experience, so the address, hours, and phone number should match everywhere they appear.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a separate page for each Palm Coast section?

acceptedAnswer.text: You need a page for each active community or subdivision you sell in, and a broader service page that explains which sections and nearby cities you serve. Buyers search by subdivision and section, so each community page should name the actual roads and landmarks nearby, such as the area near Town Center or the neighborhoods along Old Kings Road. Retired communities or sold-out phases can be consolidated into an archive page, but active communities should each have their own clear page with current homes and pricing.
